_generated: Built by tools/build-alternatives.js — edit data/alternatives-taxonomy.json and data/alternatives/*.json, then run `npm run generate:alternatives`.

_schema.description: Executable at-home alternatives shown when FitShield interrupts an ordering page. Two kinds share one presentation shape: full `recipes` and lightweight `quickAlternatives`.

shared.id: Stable unique id (kebab-case). Never reused, never renumbered.
shared.title: Name (English).
shared.description: One line explaining what it is.
shared.servings: Exact number of servings the quantities produce.
shared.ingredients: Structured objects: { quantity, unit, item, note?, optional?, substituteGroup? }.
shared.steps: Ordered instructions. Must be executable by someone who has not cooked it before.
shared.totalMinutes: Elapsed time from starting to eating.
shared.equipment: Equipment vocabulary from taxonomy.equipment. [] means no equipment at all.
shared.diet: The strictest diet this satisfies: vegan | vegetarian | pescatarian | omnivore.
shared.allergens: Major allergens present, from taxonomy.allergens. [] means none of the tracked nine.
shared.substitutions: [{ for, use }] realistic swaps, required when an ingredient is uncommon.
shared.storage: Leftover / storage guidance, or how long it keeps.
shared.region: Cuisine grouping (taxonomy.regions). Not a claim of authenticity.
shared.noCook: True when nothing is heated at all.
shared.microwave: True when a microwave alone is enough.
shared.airFryer: True when an air fryer is the primary appliance.
shared.onePan: True when cooking happens in one pan/tray.
shared.pantryFriendly: True when most ingredients are shelf-stable or freezer staples.
shared.calorieRange: [low, high] per serving, an honest RANGE or omitted. Never a single fake-precise number.

recipes.title: Naan Pizza
recipes.description: A personal pizza on naan with a properly crisp base, out of the oven in fifteen minutes.
steps: Heat the oven to 230 C / 450 F and put a baking tray in while it heats.
Brush the edges of each naan with olive oil and spread 1/4 cup of sauce over each, leaving a 1 cm border.
Scatter the mozzarella and any toppings evenly, then sprinkle with oregano.
Slide the naans onto the hot tray and bake 8-10 minutes, until the cheese is fully melted with a few browned spots and the edges are firm and dry to the touch.
Rest 2 minutes before slicing so the cheese sets.

substitutions.use: pita, a flour tortilla, or a split English muffin — reduce baking to 6-8 minutes for thinner bases
passata or crushed tinned tomatoes with a pinch of salt

recipes.storage: Best eaten straight away. Leftovers keep 2 days covered in the fridge; re-crisp in a dry pan rather than a microwave.

recipes.title: Crispy Tortilla Pizza
recipes.description: The fastest pizza-shaped thing you can make — thin, crisp, and done in a frying pan.
steps: Put a dry frying pan on medium heat for 1 minute, then add the olive oil and swirl to coat.
Lay the tortilla in flat and spread the sauce over it, leaving a 1 cm border.
Scatter the cheese over the sauce and cover the pan with a lid or a plate.
Cook 4-6 minutes without moving it. It is ready when the cheese is fully melted and the underside is golden brown — lift an edge with a spatula to check.
Slide onto a board, sprinkle with oregano, and cut into quarters.

substitutions.use: pita bread or a wrap; corn tortillas work but crisp faster, so check at 3 minutes
any melting cheese — cheddar, gouda, or a dairy-free shred

recipes.storage: Eat immediately; it softens as it cools.

recipes.title: Stovetop Smash Burger
recipes.description: Thin, deeply browned patties with crisp edges — the part of a drive-thru burger that is actually good.

ingredients.item: burger sauce or mayo and ketchup mixed

steps: Divide the beef into 4 loose balls. Do not season yet and do not compact them.
Toast the cut sides of the buns in a dry pan for 1 minute until golden, then set aside.
Put the same pan on high heat with the oil until it shimmers — about 2 minutes.
Add 2 beef balls and immediately press each flat with a spatula to about 1 cm thick. Season the tops with half the salt and pepper.
Cook 2 minutes without moving, until the edges are deep brown and lacy. Flip, add a slice of cheese, and cook 1 more minute.
Repeat with the remaining 2 balls. Cook ground beef right through — no pink in the middle.
Stack two patties per bun and add pickles and sauce.

substitutions.use: ground turkey or chicken — cook until no longer pink and the juices run clear
any bread roll, a folded flatbread, or toast

recipes.storage: Cooked patties keep 2 days in the fridge. Reheat in a pan, not a microwave, to keep the crust.

recipes.title: Black Bean Burger
recipes.description: A firm, savoury bean patty that holds together properly — the fix for most homemade veggie burgers.
steps: Pat the drained beans dry with a tea towel — wet beans are why bean burgers fall apart.
Mash about three quarters of them to a paste in a bowl, leaving the rest whole for texture.
Mix in the breadcrumbs, egg, onion, cumin, paprika, and salt until it holds together when squeezed. If it still feels wet, add breadcrumbs a tablespoon at a time.
Shape into 2 patties about 2 cm thick and chill them for 5 minutes if you have time.
Heat the oil in a frying pan over medium heat and cook the patties 4-5 minutes per side, until a firm dark crust forms and they no longer feel soft in the centre.
Serve in toasted buns with lettuce.

substitutions.use: 2 tbsp ground flaxseed mixed with 3 tbsp water, left 5 minutes — makes it vegan
rolled oats blitzed briefly, or crushed crackers
kidney beans or brown lentils, drained well

recipes.storage: Uncooked patties freeze well for 2 months. Cooked patties keep 3 days in the fridge.

recipes.title: Air Fryer Potato Wedges
recipes.description: Crisp outside, fluffy inside, with the seasoning you actually wanted from the drive-thru.
steps: Cut the potatoes into wedges about 2 cm thick at the widest point so they cook evenly.
Rinse the wedges in cold water and dry them thoroughly — surface starch and water both stop them crisping.
Toss with the oil, salt, paprika, and garlic powder until every piece is coated.
Air fry at 200 C / 400 F for 18-20 minutes, shaking the basket at the halfway point.
They are done when the outsides are deep golden and a knife slides into the thickest wedge with no resistance.

substitutions.use: a hot oven at 220 C / 425 F on a tray for 30-35 minutes, turning once

recipes.storage: Keeps 2 days; re-crisp in the air fryer for 4 minutes.

recipes.title: Air Fryer Crispy Chicken
recipes.description: Craggy, properly crunchy chicken thighs without a pot of oil.
steps: Soak the chicken in the buttermilk for at least 10 minutes while you set everything else up.
Mix the flour, salt, paprika, garlic powder, and pepper in a bowl. Spoon 2 tbsp of the buttermilk into the flour and rub it in with your fingers — the little clumps are what become the crunchy bits.
Lift each piece out letting the excess drip off, then press it firmly into the flour on all sides.
Arrange in a single layer in the air fryer basket with space between pieces, and brush or spray the tops with oil.
Air fry at 200 C / 400 F for 12 minutes, then turn, brush again, and cook 6-8 minutes more.
It is done when the coating is deep golden and the thickest piece reaches 74 C / 165 F on a thermometer, or the juices run completely clear with no pink at the bone line.
Rest 3 minutes before eating.

substitutions.use: plain yogurt thinned with milk, or milk with 1 tsp lemon juice left 5 minutes
oven at 220 C / 425 F on a wire rack for 30-35 minutes, turning once
chicken breast cut into strips — check for 74 C / 165 F from 12 minutes as it cooks faster

recipes.storage: Keeps 3 days in the fridge. Re-crisp in the air fryer at 180 C / 350 F for 5 minutes; the microwave makes it soggy.

recipes.title: Oven Cornflake Chicken Tenders
recipes.description: Loud, crunchy tenders from the oven — the closest thing to a takeaway tender without frying.
steps: Heat the oven to 220 C / 425 F and line a tray with baking paper.
Set out three shallow bowls: flour mixed with the salt and paprika, the beaten egg, and the crushed cornflakes.
Coat each strip in flour, then egg, then press firmly into the cornflakes so they stick.
Lay the strips on the tray without touching and drizzle with the olive oil.
Bake 15-18 minutes, turning once at 10 minutes.
They are done when the coating is golden and the thickest strip reads 74 C / 165 F, or is white all the way through with clear juices.

substitutions.use: panko breadcrumbs, crushed crackers, or crushed tortilla chips
3 tbsp plain yogurt or mayonnaise brushed on before coating

recipes.storage: Keeps 3 days. Reheat in a hot oven for 6 minutes to bring the crunch back.

recipes.title: Crispy Chicken Sandwich
recipes.description: A hot, crunchy chicken sandwich built the way the chains build it — pickles, sauce, soft bun.
steps: Flatten each breast between two sheets of baking paper until it is an even 1.5 cm thick — this is what stops the outside burning before the middle cooks.
Season the flour with the salt and cayenne. Coat each breast in flour, then egg, then panko, pressing hard.
Heat the oil in a frying pan over medium heat until a breadcrumb sizzles steadily when dropped in.
Fry 4-5 minutes per side without moving. The crust should be deep golden.

Check the thickest part reads 74 C / 165 F, or cut in and confirm it is white throughout with clear juices. If the crust is dark but the centre is not done, finish it in a 190 C / 375 F oven for 5 minutes.
Drain on kitchen paper for 1 minute, then build: toasted bun, mayonnaise, chicken, pickles.

substitutions.use: ordinary dried breadcrumbs or crushed cornflakes
a firm block of tofu pressed dry, or a large portobello mushroom, for a vegetarian version

recipes.storage: Fry the chicken up to a day ahead and re-crisp in a hot oven for 8 minutes; assemble just before eating.

recipes.title: Air Fryer Buffalo Wings
recipes.description: Crisp-skinned wings tossed in hot butter sauce, with no deep fryer involved.

ingredients.note: aluminium-free; this is what crisps the skin

steps: Dry the wings thoroughly with kitchen paper — any surface moisture stops them crisping.
Toss with the baking powder and salt until evenly dusted.
Air fry at 190 C / 375 F for 12 minutes, then turn and cook at 200 C / 400 F for 8-10 minutes more.
They are done when the skin is blistered and deep golden and the thickest wing reads 74 C / 165 F.
Melt the butter with the hot sauce and honey in a small pan or the microwave, then toss the hot wings through it and serve immediately.

substitutions.use: oven at 230 C / 450 F on a wire rack for 40-45 minutes, turning twice
olive oil or a dairy-free spread

recipes.storage: Best fresh. Keeps 2 days; re-crisp at 200 C / 400 F for 5 minutes.

recipes.title: Crispy Chickpea Bowl
recipes.description: A crunchy, savoury bowl for a fried-chicken craving. This is a plant substitute, not a chicken dish.
steps: Dry the chickpeas well in a tea towel; damp chickpeas steam instead of crisping.
Toss them with the oil, paprika, garlic powder, and salt.

Cook in a dry frying pan over medium-high heat for 10-12 minutes, shaking every couple of minutes. They are ready when they rattle in the pan, look wrinkled and dark golden, and split with a crack when pressed.
Thin the tahini with the lemon juice and 2-3 tbsp of water until it pours.
Build the bowls: rice, cabbage, hot chickpeas, then the sauce over the top.

substitutions.use: plain yogurt with lemon (not vegan), or a spoon of peanut butter loosened with water
couscous, a wrap, or salad leaves alone

recipes.storage: The chickpeas soften once stored; eat them the same day. The rice and sauce keep 3 days.

recipes.title: Skillet Chicken Tacos
recipes.description: Seasoned chicken, charred tortillas, and fresh toppings in twenty minutes.
steps: Toss the diced chicken with the cumin, paprika, garlic powder, and salt.
Heat the oil in a frying pan over medium-high heat until it shimmers.
Add the chicken in a single layer and leave it undisturbed for 3 minutes to brown, then stir and cook 4-5 minutes more.
It is done when no piece shows pink inside and the juices run clear — 74 C / 165 F if you have a thermometer.
Warm the tortillas 20 seconds per side in a dry pan until they puff slightly and smell toasted.
Fill with chicken, onion, and coriander, and squeeze lime over each one.

substitutions.use: flour tortillas, or lettuce leaves for a lighter version
prawns (3-4 minutes total) or firm tofu cubes

recipes.storage: The chicken keeps 3 days in the fridge and reheats well in a pan.

recipes.title: Smoky Black Bean Tacos
recipes.description: Cheap, fast, and genuinely good — tinned beans cooked down until they are thick and smoky.
steps: Heat the oil in a small pan over medium heat, add the cumin and paprika, and stir for 30 seconds until they smell toasted.
Add the beans, salt, and water. Cook 5-6 minutes, mashing about a third of the beans against the pan, until the mixture is thick enough to hold a line when you drag a spoon through it.
Warm the tortillas 20 seconds per side in a dry pan.
Fill with beans, cheese, and salsa, and finish with a squeeze of lime.

substitutions.use: sliced avocado or a dairy-free shred — leave it out entirely and the recipe is vegan
pinto or kidney beans

recipes.storage: The bean mix keeps 4 days and freezes well.

recipes.title: Bean and Rice Burrito
recipes.description: A proper full-size burrito built from pantry staples and folded so it does not fall apart.
steps: Stir the cumin and salt through the warm beans.
Warm each tortilla for 20-30 seconds in a dry pan until soft and pliable — a cold tortilla will split when rolled.
Pile the filling in a line across the lower third of the tortilla, leaving 5 cm clear at each side. Do not overfill.
Fold the two sides in, then roll the bottom edge up and over the filling, pulling back gently to tighten as you roll.
Toast the finished burrito seam-side down in a dry pan over medium heat for 2 minutes per side, until the outside is golden and sealed.

substitutions.use: a microwave rice pouch, or leave the rice out and use more beans
a dairy-free shred; skip the sour cream and this is vegan

recipes.storage: Wrap in foil and refrigerate up to 3 days, or freeze for 2 months. Reheat wrapped in the oven at 180 C / 350 F for 20 minutes.

recipes.title: Breakfast Burrito
recipes.description: Eggs, cheese, and potato in a tortilla — filling, cheap, and freezes for later.

ingredients.item: frozen diced potatoes or hash browns

steps: Cook the frozen potatoes in a dry non-stick pan over medium-high heat for 6-8 minutes without stirring much, until browned and crisp at the edges. Tip onto a plate.
Lower the heat to medium-low, melt the butter, and add the eggs beaten with the salt.

Stir slowly and constantly with a spatula for 2-3 minutes, until the egg forms soft curds that hold their shape and are no longer runny. Take them off while they still look slightly wet — they finish cooking in the pan's heat.
Warm the tortillas 20 seconds per side, then fill with potato, egg, cheese, and salsa.
Fold the sides in and roll tightly, then toast seam-side down for 2 minutes.

substitutions.for: frozen diced potatoes or hash browns
substitutions.use: a tin of black beans, drained, warmed with cumin
any cooking oil

recipes.storage: Wrap in foil and freeze up to 2 months. Reheat from frozen in the microwave for 3 minutes, turning once.

recipes.title: Crispy Tofu Tacos
recipes.description: Crumbled tofu browned hard until it has real texture, then seasoned like taco meat.
steps: Wrap the tofu in a tea towel and press under something heavy for 10 minutes, then crumble it into rough pieces.
Heat the oil in a frying pan over medium-high heat and add the tofu in one layer.
Cook 8-10 minutes, stirring only every 2-3 minutes. Wait until the pieces are golden and firm rather than pale and soft — this is the whole difference.
Add the cumin, paprika, soy sauce, and salt and toss for 1 minute more.
Warm the tortillas, then fill with tofu, cabbage, lime, and hot sauce.

substitutions.use: a tin of drained, dried chickpeas, roughly crushed
tamari for a gluten-free version, or 0.25 tsp extra salt

recipes.storage: Keeps 3 days; re-crisp in a hot dry pan.

recipes.title: Egg Fried Rice
recipes.description: The takeaway staple, and genuinely better with day-old rice from your own fridge.

ingredients.note: cold, ideally from the day before

steps: Break up any clumps in the cold rice with your fingers before you start — this is the single biggest difference between good and gluey fried rice.
Heat 1 tbsp of oil in a large pan or wok over high heat, pour in the eggs, and scramble them for 45 seconds until just set. Tip onto a plate.
Add the remaining oil, then the garlic and frozen vegetables. Cook 2 minutes until the vegetables are hot and any water has boiled off.
Add the rice and press it into the pan. Leave it 1 minute to catch, then toss. Repeat twice more over about 4 minutes until you can hear it crackling.
Return the egg, add the soy sauce and sesame oil, and toss for 1 minute.
Take off the heat and scatter over the spring onions.

substitutions.use: a microwave rice pouch cooked and cooled for 5 minutes, or leftover noodles
tamari for gluten-free
cubed firm tofu browned first — makes it vegan

recipes.storage: Keeps 2 days. Reheat until piping hot throughout; cooked rice should be cooled quickly and never left at room temperature for long.

recipes.title: Garlic Soy Noodles
recipes.description: Ten minutes, five pantry ingredients, and a sauce that clings properly to the noodles.

ingredients.note: egg, wheat, or instant noodle blocks without the sachet

steps: Boil the noodles for the time on the packet, then drain, keeping 4 tbsp of the cooking water.
While they cook, mix the soy sauce, sesame oil, and sugar in a bowl.

Heat the neutral oil in a pan over medium heat and cook the garlic for 45-60 seconds, until it smells sweet and turns pale gold. Take it off the moment it colours — burnt garlic turns the whole dish bitter.

Add the drained noodles, the sauce, and 2 tbsp of the reserved water. Toss over the heat for 1 minute until the sauce coats every strand and no liquid pools in the pan; add the rest of the water if it looks dry.
Finish with chilli flakes and spring onions.

substitutions.use: spaghetti — it works better than people expect
tamari for gluten-free, with rice noodles

recipes.storage: Keeps 2 days; loosen with a splash of water when reheating.

recipes.title: Chicken Teriyaki Rice Bowl
recipes.description: Glossy, sweet-savoury chicken over rice, with a sauce you make from four things you already have.
steps: Mix the soy sauce, honey, vinegar, and ginger in a small bowl.
Heat the oil in a frying pan over medium-high heat and add the chicken in one layer. Leave it 3 minutes to brown before stirring.
Cook 5-6 minutes more, stirring, until every piece is browned and cooked through — no pink inside, 74 C / 165 F if you have a thermometer.
Steam or microwave the frozen vegetables until hot, about 3 minutes.
Pour the sauce into the pan with the chicken. It will bubble hard; keep stirring for 60-90 seconds until it thickens to a syrup that coats the pieces.
Serve over rice with the vegetables and a scatter of sesame seeds.

substitutions.use: any mild vinegar, or a squeeze of lemon
firm tofu cubes browned hard first, for a vegan bowl with honey swapped for sugar

recipes.storage: Keeps 3 days in the fridge and reheats well in a pan or microwave.

recipes.title: Kimchi Fried Rice
recipes.description: Sharp, spicy, and deeply savoury — a quick-style bowl built around a jar of kimchi.

ingredients.note: roughly chopped, plus 3 tbsp of its juice

steps: Heat the oil in a large pan over medium-high heat and cook the chopped kimchi for 3 minutes until the edges start to caramelise and it smells sweeter than raw.
Stir in the kimchi juice, and the gochujang if you are using it, and cook 30 seconds.
Add the cold rice, breaking up clumps, and press it flat. Leave 1 minute, toss, and repeat for about 4 minutes until heated through with crisp patches.
Stir through the sesame oil and take off the heat.
If using eggs, fry them separately for 2-3 minutes until the whites are fully set, and slide one on top of each bowl.

substitutions.use: 1 tsp chilli flakes with 1 tsp tomato paste and a pinch of sugar
sauerkraut with 1 tsp chilli flakes — different, but the same sharp-savoury effect
leave them out for a vegan bowl; check your kimchi has no fish sauce

recipes.storage: Keeps 2 days. Reheat until piping hot.

recipes.title: Peanut Noodles
recipes.description: A rich, satisfying sauce whisked together in a bowl while the noodles boil.
steps: Boil the noodles over high heat for the time on the packet, usually 4-6 minutes, until tender with a slight bite. Reserve half a cup of the water before draining.
Whisk the peanut butter, soy sauce, vinegar, sugar, and garlic in a large bowl. It will seize and look wrong at first.
Add the hot noodle water 1 tbsp at a time, whisking, until the sauce becomes smooth and just thin enough to pour.
Toss the drained noodles through the sauce until every strand is coated.
Top with the shredded vegetables and chilli flakes.

substitutions.use: tahini or sunflower seed butter for a peanut-free version
spaghetti or rice noodles

recipes.storage: Keeps 2 days; the sauce thickens cold, so loosen with hot water.

recipes.title: Quick-Style Chana Masala
recipes.description: A simplified weeknight version of the chickpea curry — twenty minutes from a tin, not a takeaway.
steps: Heat the oil in a saucepan over medium heat and cook the onion for 6-7 minutes, stirring now and then, until it is soft and the edges are golden.
Add the garlic and ginger and cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Add the cumin, coriander, and turmeric and stir for 30 seconds — the spices should smell toasted, not raw or burnt.
Tip in the tomatoes and salt. Simmer 8 minutes, until the sauce darkens and thickens enough that a spoon dragged through leaves a brief trail.
Add the chickpeas and simmer 4 minutes more, crushing a few against the side of the pan to thicken the sauce.
Take off the heat and stir in the garam masala and lemon juice.

substitutions.use: a curry powder blend; add it with the other spices instead of at the end
any tinned bean, or red lentils with an extra cup of water and 15 minutes

recipes.storage: Better the next day. Keeps 4 days in the fridge and freezes for 3 months.

recipes.title: Red Lentil Dal
recipes.description: Cheap, comforting, and hands-off — the lentils cook themselves while you do nothing.

ingredients.note: rinsed until the water runs clear

steps: Put the rinsed lentils, water, turmeric, and salt in a saucepan and bring to the boil.
Skim off any foam, lower the heat, and simmer uncovered for 15-18 minutes, stirring occasionally.
It is ready when the lentils have completely lost their shape and the dal coats the back of a spoon. Add a splash more water if it gets too thick.
In a small pan, heat the butter over medium heat, add the cumin seeds, and wait for them to sizzle and pop — about 30 seconds.
Add the garlic and chilli flakes and cook 45 seconds until the garlic is pale gold. Take it off before it browns.
Pour the hot spiced butter over the dal, stir once, and finish with lemon juice.

substitutions.use: any oil, which makes the dal vegan
0.75 tsp ground cumin, added to the garlic rather than heated alone
yellow split lentils (moong dal), with 10 minutes more simmering

recipes.storage: Keeps 4 days and freezes for 3 months. It thickens in the fridge; loosen with water when reheating.

recipes.title: Paneer Bhurji
recipes.description: Crumbled paneer cooked with onion and spices — a fast, high-protein alternative to a curry order.
steps: Heat the oil in a frying pan over medium heat and cook the onion 5 minutes until soft and translucent.
Add the cumin, turmeric, and chilli powder and stir for 30 seconds.
Add the tomato and salt and cook 3-4 minutes, pressing with the spoon, until it breaks down into a thick paste and the oil starts to separate at the edges.
Stir in the crumbled paneer and cook 3 minutes, just long enough to heat it through. Cooking it longer makes it rubbery.
Finish with coriander and serve with warm flatbread.

substitutions.use: firm tofu, pressed and crumbled, for a vegan version; or 4 beaten eggs stirred in at the end
rice, or any bread you have

recipes.storage: Keeps 2 days; reheat gently so the paneer stays soft.

recipes.title: Shawarma-Style Chicken Wrap
recipes.description: Inspired by shawarma, not a copy of it — spiced chicken in a pan, wrapped with garlic yogurt.
steps: Toss the sliced chicken with the cumin, paprika, coriander, cinnamon, salt, and 1 tbsp of the oil.
Mix the yogurt, garlic, lemon juice, and a pinch of salt in a small bowl and set aside.
Heat the remaining oil in a frying pan over medium-high heat and spread the chicken out in one layer.
Leave it 3 minutes to brown, then stir and cook 4-5 minutes more until the pieces are browned at the edges and cooked through with no pink inside.
Warm the flatbreads for 20 seconds a side, spread with garlic yogurt, add the chicken and salad, and roll up tightly.

substitutions.use: a dairy-free yogurt, or plain hummus
sliced halloumi, or a tin of chickpeas roasted with the same spices

recipes.storage: The cooked chicken keeps 3 days; assemble wraps fresh.

recipes.title: Crispy Chickpea Falafel-Style Patties
recipes.description: A simplified pan-fried take on falafel — same herbs and spices, no deep frying, no overnight soak.
steps: Dry the chickpeas properly in a tea towel. Wet chickpeas make a paste that will not hold.

Pulse the chickpeas, herbs, garlic, flour, spices, and salt in a food processor to a coarse, crumbly mixture that holds when squeezed — stop before it becomes smooth. With no processor, mash by hand and chop the herbs finely.
Shape into 6 flat patties about 1.5 cm thick.
Heat the oil in a frying pan over medium heat and fry 3-4 minutes per side, until deeply golden and firm.
Serve in warm pita with hummus and salad.

substitutions.use: chickpea flour or fine breadcrumbs; gluten-free flour works too
tahini loosened with lemon and water, or plain yogurt if not vegan

recipes.storage: Keeps 3 days; re-crisp in a dry pan. Uncooked patties freeze for 2 months.

recipes.title: Garlic Butter Spaghetti
recipes.description: Four ingredients, ten minutes, and a sauce that clings because of the pasta water.
steps: Boil the spaghetti in well-salted water for the time on the packet, and scoop out a mugful of the water before draining.
While it boils, melt the butter in a wide pan over medium-low heat and add the garlic and chilli flakes.
Cook the garlic gently for 2-3 minutes until it is pale gold and smells sweet. If it browns it will taste bitter, so keep the heat low.
Add the drained pasta and 0.5 cup of the pasta water to the pan and toss hard over medium heat for 60-90 seconds.
The sauce is ready when it turns glossy and coats the strands instead of pooling. Add more pasta water a splash at a time if it looks dry.
Take off the heat, stir in the parmesan and parsley, and serve immediately.

substitutions.use: olive oil, which makes it vegan if you also skip the parmesan
any hard cheese, or nutritional yeast

recipes.storage: Best fresh. Keeps 2 days; reheat with a splash of water.

recipes.title: One-Pan Tomato Pasta
recipes.description: Pasta cooked directly in the sauce — one pan, no colander, and a thicker result.
steps: Heat the oil in a wide deep pan over medium heat and cook the garlic for 45 seconds until fragrant.
Add the tomatoes, water, oregano, salt, and the dry pasta. Stir well and bring to the boil.
Simmer uncovered for 12-14 minutes, stirring every 2 minutes so nothing sticks to the bottom.
It is done when the pasta is tender with a slight bite and the liquid has reduced to a sauce that clings. Add a splash of water if it thickens too fast.
Take off the heat, stir in the cheese, and tear the basil over the top.

substitutions.use: 1.5 cups of tomato pasta sauce with 1.5 cups water
leave it out for a vegan pan

recipes.storage: Keeps 3 days. It thickens cold; loosen with water when reheating.

recipes.title: Grilled Cheese and Tomato Soup
recipes.description: The most reliable comfort meal there is, done properly: low heat, real browning.
steps: Butter the outside face of each slice of bread, right to the edges.
Build two sandwiches with the cheese inside and the buttered sides facing out.
Put them in a cold frying pan, then turn the heat to medium-LOW. Starting cold is what lets the cheese melt before the bread burns.
Cook 4-5 minutes per side, pressing gently, until each side is evenly deep golden and the cheese is visibly molten at the edges.
Heat the soup in a saucepan over medium heat for 4-5 minutes, stirring, until steaming.
Cut the sandwiches diagonally and serve with the soup.

substitutions.use: any tinned soup, or tinned tomatoes blitzed with a pinch of sugar and salt
mayonnaise on the outside — it browns beautifully — or a dairy-free spread

recipes.storage: Eat the sandwich straight away; leftover soup keeps 3 days.

recipes.title: Caprese Sandwich
recipes.description: Mozzarella, tomato, and basil pressed into good bread. Nothing is cooked.
steps: Salt the tomato slices lightly and leave them on kitchen paper for 2 minutes, then pat dry — this stops the bread going soggy.
Drizzle the cut faces of the roll with olive oil.
Layer mozzarella, tomato, and basil, then season with salt, pepper, and balsamic.
Close the sandwich and press down firmly with your palm for 10 seconds before cutting.

substitutions.use: any soft cheese, or sliced avocado for a vegan sandwich
ciabatta, sourdough, or a baguette section

recipes.storage: Eat within a couple of hours; it does not keep well.

recipes.title: Greek Salad Pita
recipes.description: A crunchy, salty, no-cook pita that eats like a proper meal.
steps: Toss the cucumber, tomato, onion, and olives with the olive oil, lemon juice, and oregano.
Let it sit 3 minutes so the vegetables release a little juice and the dressing loosens.
Warm the pitas for 20 seconds each side in a dry pan or toaster so they open without tearing.
Stir the feta through the salad, then stuff the pitas, spooning a little of the dressing in last.

substitutions.use: a firm dairy-free cheese, or a tin of drained chickpeas for a vegan pita
a tortilla wrap, or eat it as a salad with no bread at all

recipes.storage: The salad keeps 2 days undressed; assemble the pitas fresh.

recipes.title: Soft Scrambled Eggs on Toast
recipes.description: Five minutes, two ingredients, and the one technique that separates creamy from rubbery.
steps: Beat the eggs with the salt until no streaks of white remain.
Put the toast on.
Melt the butter in a non-stick pan over LOW heat — low is the whole trick.
Pour in the eggs and stir slowly and constantly with a spatula, scraping the base every few seconds.
After 2-3 minutes they will start forming soft curds. Take the pan off the heat while they still look slightly wet and glossy; the residual heat finishes them.
Pile onto the toast and grind pepper over.

substitutions.use: olive oil or any spread
a tortilla, a bagel, or nothing at all

recipes.storage: Eat immediately; scrambled eggs do not keep well.

recipes.title: Overnight Oats
recipes.description: Two minutes tonight, breakfast handled tomorrow. Nothing is cooked.
steps: Stir the oats, milk, yogurt, and sweetener together in a jar or bowl.
The mixture should look far too wet — the oats absorb most of it overnight.
Cover and refrigerate at least 4 hours, ideally overnight.
In the morning, stir, add a splash more milk if it is stiff, and top with fruit and peanut butter.

substitutions.use: any plant milk, which makes it vegan if you also skip the yogurt and honey
any seed butter, or leave it out

recipes.storage: Keeps 3 days in the fridge, so make several at once.

recipes.title: Iced Latte
recipes.description: The coffee-shop drink, at home, for the price of the beans.
steps: If you are sweetening it, stir the sugar into the hot coffee first — it will not dissolve once the drink is cold.
Cool the coffee: either brew it ahead, or pour it over 3-4 ice cubes and stir for 20 seconds, then discard those cubes.
Fill a tall glass with fresh ice and pour the milk in.
Pour the cooled coffee slowly over the back of a spoon so it layers, then stir before drinking.

substitutions.use: oat milk froths best of the plant milks and keeps this vegan
1 tbsp instant coffee dissolved in 60 ml hot water

recipes.storage: Brew a jug of coffee and keep it in the fridge for 3 days to make this a 60-second drink.

recipes.title: Blended Mocha
recipes.description: The thick, sweet, blended coffee drink — made in a blender in three minutes.
steps: Whisk the cocoa, sugar, and salt into the warm coffee until completely smooth — cocoa will not blend out of lumps later.
Let it cool for a minute, then add it to the blender with the milk and ice.
Blend on high for 30-45 seconds, until there are no ice shards left and the drink pours thickly.
If it is too thin, add 3-4 more ice cubes and blend 10 seconds more.

substitutions.use: any plant milk for a vegan drink
2 tbsp drinking chocolate, and drop the sugar to 1 tsp

recipes.storage: Drink immediately; it separates as it melts.

recipes.title: Berry Protein Smoothie
recipes.description: A thick, cold smoothie that actually fills you up. This is a drink, not a coffee substitute.
steps: Put the liquid in the blender first — this is what stops the blades jamming on frozen fruit.
Add the banana, then the frozen berries, then the protein powder or yogurt on top.
Blend 45-60 seconds until completely smooth with no visible fruit pieces.
If the blender stalls, stop and stir the mixture down rather than adding more liquid.

substitutions.use: 3 tbsp yogurt, or 2 tbsp oats for body
any plant milk, making it vegan if you skip the yogurt

recipes.storage: Drink fresh. Pre-bag the fruit in the freezer to make this a 90-second job.

recipes.title: Microwave Mug Brownie
recipes.description: A single warm, fudgy brownie in ninety seconds, with no oven and nothing left over.
steps: Mix the flour, sugar, cocoa, and salt in a large microwave-safe mug with a fork until no cocoa streaks remain.
Add the milk, oil, and vanilla and stir until smooth, scraping the bottom corners of the mug where dry flour hides.
Microwave on full power for 60 seconds, then check: the top should look set and matt but the very centre should still be soft.
If it is still wet on top, give it 10-second bursts. Stop as soon as the top is set — overcooking by even 20 seconds turns it rubbery.
Let it stand 2 minutes before eating; it is extremely hot straight out.

substitutions.use: water works, though it is less rich
a gluten-free flour blend, cooked 15 seconds longer

recipes.storage: Eat immediately; it goes dense once cold.

recipes.title: Banana Ice Cream
recipes.description: Two frozen bananas blended into something genuinely like soft-serve. One ingredient, no churning.

ingredients.note: sliced and frozen at least 3 hours
only if the blender needs help

steps: Take the frozen banana out and let it sit for 3-4 minutes — rock-hard fruit will stall a blender.
Blend on high. It will go through a crumbly stage that looks wrong; keep going.
After 45-90 seconds it suddenly turns smooth, thick, and glossy. That is the point to stop.
Only add milk a teaspoon at a time if the blender genuinely cannot move; too much makes it a smoothie.
Blend in the cocoa or peanut butter for 10 seconds and serve straight away, or freeze 30 minutes for a firmer scoop.

substitutions.use: frozen mango chunks, blended the same way, with a splash more liquid
any nut or seed butter, or leave it out

recipes.storage: Freezes solid; let it soften 10 minutes before scooping again.

recipes.title: Cinnamon Sugar Toast
recipes.description: A bakery-counter craving answered with bread, butter, and sugar under the grill.
steps: Heat the grill or a toaster oven to high.
Mix the sugar and cinnamon together in a small bowl.
Spread the butter thickly right to the edges of the bread, then press the cinnamon sugar evenly over the top.
Grill 2-3 minutes, watching it the whole time. It is ready when the sugar has melted, bubbled, and just begun to darken at the edges.
Let it cool 1 minute — melted sugar is dangerously hot — then cut into fingers.

substitutions.use: a dairy-free spread, which makes it vegan
a dry frying pan, butter-side down, over medium heat for 2-3 minutes

recipes.storage: Eat straight away.

recipes.title: Tinned Salmon Patties
recipes.description: Crisp, savoury fish cakes from a tin and a few pantry things — ready in twenty minutes.
steps: Drain the salmon thoroughly and flake it with a fork, breaking up any soft bones — they are edible and add calcium.
Mix with the egg, breadcrumbs, spring onions, lemon juice, salt, and pepper until it holds together when pressed.
Shape into 4 patties about 2 cm thick and rest them 5 minutes so the breadcrumbs absorb the moisture.
Heat the oil in a frying pan over medium heat and cook 3-4 minutes per side, until a firm golden crust forms and they are hot right through.
Serve with mayonnaise and a lemon wedge.

substitutions.use: two tins of tuna, drained very well
crushed crackers, instant mashed potato, or rolled oats

recipes.storage: Keeps 2 days in the fridge; reheat in a pan to keep the crust.

recipes.title: Loaded Chopped Salad
recipes.description: A salad with enough protein and crunch to actually be dinner, dressed in the bowl.
steps: Whisk the olive oil, lemon juice, mustard, and salt in the bottom of a large bowl until it thickens slightly and stops separating.
Add the chickpeas and the diced cucumber and tomato and toss — the firm things go in first so they take the dressing.
Chop the leaves smaller than feels necessary; a chopped salad works because every forkful gets everything.
Add the leaves and cheese and toss just before serving so nothing wilts.
Top with croutons or nuts for crunch.

substitutions.use: leave it out and add half an avocado, for a vegan salad
leftover cooked chicken, or a tin of tuna

recipes.storage: Keeps 2 days undressed. Dress only what you are eating now.

recipes.title: Crispy Tofu Sandwich
recipes.description: A plant substitute for a crispy chicken sandwich — same crunch, same pickles, same soft bun.

ingredients.note: pressed and cut into 2 thick slabs

steps: Press the tofu between two plates under something heavy for 10 minutes, then cut into 2 slabs about 2 cm thick. Wet tofu will never crisp.
Set out three shallow bowls: the flour mixed with salt, paprika, and garlic powder; the plant milk; and the panko.
Coat each slab in flour, then milk, then press hard into the panko so it holds a thick, craggy layer.
Heat the oil in a frying pan over medium heat until a breadcrumb sizzles steadily when dropped in.
Fry 4-5 minutes per side without moving. It is ready when the crust is deep golden and firm enough to tap with a spatula.
Drain on kitchen paper for 1 minute, then build: toasted bun, mayonnaise, tofu, pickles.

substitutions.use: ordinary dried breadcrumbs or crushed cornflakes
two large portobello mushrooms, or halloumi if you are not vegan
any milk, or 3 tbsp plain yogurt loosened with water

recipes.storage: Fry up to a day ahead and re-crisp in a hot oven for 8 minutes; assemble just before eating.

recipes.title: Buffalo Cauliflower Bites
recipes.description: A plant alternative to hot wings — battered, crisped, and tossed in the same buffalo sauce.

ingredients.note: about 600 g, cut into bite-sized florets

steps: Whisk the flour, plant milk, garlic powder, and salt into a batter about as thick as single cream.
Toss the florets through it, lifting each one out so the excess drips back — a thick coat steams instead of crisping.
Arrange in a single layer in the air fryer basket with gaps between them and brush with the neutral oil.
Air fry at 190 C / 375 F for 14 minutes, shaking at the halfway point.
Turn up to 200 C / 400 F for 5-6 minutes more. They are done when the coating is dry to the touch, golden, and crisp at the edges.
Whisk the hot sauce, olive oil, and maple syrup together, toss the hot florets through it, and eat straight away.

substitutions.use: oven at 220 C / 425 F on a lined tray for 30-35 minutes, turning once
water works, or any milk if you are not vegan

recipes.storage: Best straight away; the coating softens within an hour.

recipes.title: Quick Vegetable Dumplings
recipes.description: Shop-bought wrappers, a cabbage and mushroom filling, and a crisp-bottomed pan finish.
steps: Toss the cabbage with the salt and leave it 5 minutes, then squeeze out the water with your hands. This is what stops the wrappers going soggy.
Mix the squeezed cabbage with the mushrooms, garlic, ginger, soy sauce, and sesame oil.
Put a heaped teaspoon in the centre of each wrapper, wet the rim with water, fold over and pinch firmly shut all along the edge.
Heat the neutral oil in a frying pan with a lid over medium heat and set the dumplings flat-side down. Fry 2-3 minutes until the bottoms are golden.
Pour in the water, cover immediately, and steam 6-7 minutes until the water has gone and the wrappers look translucent and are hot right through.

substitutions.use: wonton or gyoza wrappers — check the packet, as some contain egg
grated carrot, or crumbled firm tofu

recipes.storage: Freeze uncooked on a tray, then bag. Cook from frozen with 3 extra minutes of steaming.

quickAlternatives.title: Frozen Pizza, Made Better
quickAlternatives.description: The lowest-effort pizza there is, with two small changes that close most of the gap.
steps: Heat the oven 25 C / 50 F hotter than the box says and put the shelf in the lowest position.
Add the extra cheese, then bake for the time on the box, checking 3 minutes early. It is ready when the cheese is bubbling and the crust edge is golden and firm.
Brush the crust edge with olive oil and sprinkle oregano over the top as it comes out.
quickAlternatives.storage: Leftovers keep 2 days; reheat in a dry pan with a lid.

quickAlternatives.title: Frozen Patty Cheeseburger
quickAlternatives.description: Freezer to plate in ten minutes with no defrosting and no shaping.

ingredients.item: frozen beef or plant burger patty
burger sauce or mayo and ketchup mixed

steps: Cook the patty straight from frozen in a dry pan over medium heat, 5-6 minutes per side. Beef must be cooked right through with no pink in the middle.
Add the cheese for the last minute and cover the pan so it melts.
Toast the bun cut-side down in the same pan for 1 minute, then build with sauce and pickles.

substitutions.for: frozen beef or plant burger patty
substitutions.use: a plant-based patty makes this vegetarian; check the packet cooking time

quickAlternatives.title: English Muffin Pizzas
quickAlternatives.description: Four small pizzas under the grill while the kettle is still boiling.
steps: Toast the split muffins lightly so the bases stay firm.
Spread 1 tbsp of sauce on each half and top with cheese.
Grill or bake at 220 C / 425 F for 5-6 minutes, until the cheese is bubbling with browned spots.

substitutions.use: bagel halves, crumpets, or thick sliced bread

quickAlternatives.title: Frozen Chicken Strip Wrap
quickAlternatives.description: Freezer strips, a tortilla, and sauce — hot food in twelve minutes with no prep.
steps: Cook the strips from frozen in the air fryer at 200 C / 400 F for 10 minutes, or follow the packet oven time. Check they are piping hot right through before eating.
Warm the tortilla for 20 seconds in a dry pan or microwave so it folds without cracking.
Spread the sauce, add lettuce, cheese, and the hot strips, then roll tightly and cut in half.

substitutions.use: frozen plant-based nuggets for a vegetarian version

quickAlternatives.title: Rotisserie Chicken Sandwich
quickAlternatives.description: A real chicken sandwich in five minutes, because the chicken is already cooked.
steps: Toast the bread if you want it to hold up to the mayonnaise.
Toss the pulled chicken with the mayonnaise, salt, and pepper.
Pile onto the bread with lettuce and tomato, close, and cut in half.

substitutions.use: any leftover cooked chicken, or a tin of chicken drained well
a wrap, a bun, or a pita pocket

quickAlternatives.storage: The chicken mix keeps 2 days in the fridge.

quickAlternatives.title: Microwave Rice, Beans, and Salsa
quickAlternatives.description: A hot, filling bowl in four minutes using only a microwave and three tins or pouches.
steps: Microwave the rice pouch for the time on the packet, usually 2 minutes.
Tip it into a bowl with the beans, salsa, and cumin and stir.
Microwave the bowl 90 seconds more, stir again, and check it is steaming hot throughout before adding the cheese.

substitutions.use: any leftover cooked rice, or instant couscous made with boiling water
leave it out for a vegan bowl

quickAlternatives.title: Cheese Quesadilla
quickAlternatives.description: Two ingredients, one pan, six minutes — the reliable answer to almost any craving.
steps: Put a dry frying pan on medium heat and lay the tortilla in flat.
Scatter the cheese over one half only, add any extras, and fold the empty half over.
Cook 2-3 minutes per side, pressing gently with a spatula, until both sides have golden patches and the cheese is fully melted.
Slide out, wait 1 minute so the cheese sets, then cut into wedges.

substitutions.use: a dairy-free shred, or refried beans alone

quickAlternatives.title: Microwave Nachos
quickAlternatives.description: The late-night one. Three minutes, one plate, no oven.
steps: Spread the chips in a single overlapping layer on a microwave-safe plate — piled chips steam and go soft.
Scatter the cheese and beans evenly over the top.
Microwave 45-60 seconds, until the cheese has just melted. Stop as soon as it does; longer makes the chips chewy.
Spoon over the salsa and jalapenos.

substitutions.use: a dairy-free shred for a vegan plate

quickAlternatives.title: Frozen Dumplings with Greens
quickAlternatives.description: Straight from the freezer to crisp-bottomed dumplings in twelve minutes.
steps: Heat the oil in a frying pan with a lid over medium heat and arrange the frozen dumplings flat-side down in one layer.
Fry 2-3 minutes until the bottoms are golden, then pour in the water — it will steam violently — and put the lid on straight away.
Steam 6-8 minutes until the water has gone and the dumplings are hot right through. Follow the packet time if it is longer.
Microwave or steam the greens for 3 minutes and serve alongside with soy sauce and chilli oil.

substitutions.use: vegetable dumplings for a vegetarian plate — check the packet

quickAlternatives.title: Upgraded Instant Noodles
quickAlternatives.description: The packet you already have, turned into an actual meal with an egg and something green.
steps: Boil the noodles over high heat in their water for 3 minutes, adding the frozen vegetables at the same time, until the noodles are tender and the vegetables are steaming hot.
One minute before the noodles are done, crack the egg into the pan and leave it undisturbed so it poaches, or stir it through for a silky broth.
Add the seasoning sachet off the heat — using half keeps the salt down without losing the flavour.
Finish with sesame oil and spring onion.

substitutions.use: a handful of frozen edamame or cubed tofu for a vegan bowl

quickAlternatives.title: Tinned Tuna Rice Bowl
quickAlternatives.description: A poke-shop shape built from a tin and a rice pouch, with no cooking beyond the microwave.
steps: Heat the rice pouch in the microwave for the time on the packet, usually 2 minutes, until steaming hot, then tip into a bowl.
Mix the drained tuna with the mayonnaise, soy sauce, and sriracha.
Spoon over the rice, then add the cucumber and sesame seeds if you have them.

substitutions.use: tinned salmon, or chickpeas mashed with the mayonnaise for a vegetarian bowl

quickAlternatives.storage: Eat straight away; do not leave tinned fish at room temperature.

quickAlternatives.title: Hummus Plate
quickAlternatives.description: No cooking at all — a plate of hummus, bread, and whatever crunchy things you have.
steps: Spread the hummus on a plate and make a shallow well in the middle with the back of a spoon.
Pour the olive oil into the well and dust with paprika.
Arrange the bread and vegetables around it and eat with your hands.

substitutions.use: crackers, toast, or tortilla chips

quickAlternatives.storage: Eat straight away; opened hummus keeps 3 days.

quickAlternatives.title: Microwave Dal and Rice
quickAlternatives.description: A tinned-lentil shortcut for a curry craving when the only appliance is a microwave.
steps: Stir the lentils, tomatoes, cumin, turmeric, and salt together in a microwave-safe bowl.
Microwave 2 minutes, stir, then 1 minute more until steaming hot throughout.
Heat the rice pouch for the time on the packet and serve the dal over it with the butter stirred in.

substitutions.use: 2 tbsp tomato pasta sauce or passata
oil, which makes it vegan

quickAlternatives.title: Tinned Soup and Toast
quickAlternatives.description: The lowest-effort hot meal in the house — five minutes, one pan, one toaster.
steps: Heat the soup in a saucepan over medium heat for 4-5 minutes, stirring, until it is steaming hot throughout.
Toast the bread and butter it while it is hot.
Stir the cheese into the soup off the heat if you want it richer.

substitutions.use: any tinned or carton soup; check the label if you need it vegetarian
microwave the soup in a bowl for 2-3 minutes, stirring halfway

quickAlternatives.title: Deli Turkey Sandwich
quickAlternatives.description: A cold sandwich built properly, in four minutes, with nothing switched on.
steps: Spread mayonnaise on both slices — it is a moisture barrier as much as a condiment.
Layer cheese first, then the meat, then lettuce and tomato so the wet ingredients sit away from the bread.
Add mustard, close, press gently, and cut diagonally.

substitutions.use: hummus and grated carrot, or sliced halloumi, for a vegetarian sandwich

quickAlternatives.storage: Eat within a few hours; keep refrigerated.

quickAlternatives.title: Pesto Pasta with Frozen Veg
quickAlternatives.description: One pot, two ingredients you already have, and a green vegetable that cooks itself.
steps: Boil the pasta over high heat for the time on the packet, adding the frozen vegetables for the last 3 minutes, until the pasta is tender and the vegetables are hot right through.
Reserve half a cup of the cooking water, then drain.
Return everything to the pot off the heat, stir in the pesto and 3 tbsp of the water, and toss until glossy and coated.
Add cheese if you want it richer.

substitutions.use: a nut-free or vegan pesto; check the label, as most contain pine nuts and cheese

quickAlternatives.storage: Keeps 2 days; good cold as a pasta salad.

quickAlternatives.title: Yogurt, Fruit, and Granola
quickAlternatives.description: Three things in a bowl. Two minutes, no appliances, no cooking.
steps: Spoon the yogurt into a bowl or glass.
Add the fruit, then the granola last so it stays crunchy.
Drizzle with honey if you want it sweeter.

substitutions.use: a plant yogurt, with maple syrup instead of honey, for a vegan bowl
crushed digestive biscuits, or plain oats

quickAlternatives.title: Two-Minute Iced Coffee
quickAlternatives.description: Instant coffee, ice, milk. The fastest possible answer to a coffee-shop craving.
steps: Dissolve the coffee and sugar in the hot water and stir hard for 20 seconds.
Fill a glass with ice and pour in the milk.
Pour the coffee over and stir.

substitutions.use: any plant milk for a vegan drink

quickAlternatives.title: Iced Matcha or Chai Milk
quickAlternatives.description: The non-coffee tea-shop drink, without the queue or the sugar load.
steps: For matcha: whisk the powder into the hot water for 20 seconds until no lumps remain and a light foam forms. For chai: steep the teabag in the hot water for 4 minutes, then remove it.
Stir in the sweetener while the liquid is still hot.
Fill a glass with ice, pour in the cold milk, then pour the tea over the top and stir.

substitutions.use: any strong tea — black, jasmine, or rooibos
oat milk, for a vegan drink with sugar instead of honey

quickAlternatives.title: Peanut Butter and Banana Toast
quickAlternatives.description: Three minutes, three ingredients, and enough substance to stop a craving.
steps: Toast the bread for 2-3 minutes, until firm and golden enough to hold the topping.
Spread the peanut butter while the toast is hot so it softens and spreads thinly.
Lay the banana slices over and finish with cinnamon and honey.

substitutions.use: any seed or nut butter, for a peanut-free version
maple syrup, which makes it vegan

quickAlternatives.title: Frozen Fruit Yogurt Swirl
quickAlternatives.description: Two minutes to something cold and sweet, using a tub of yogurt and the freezer.
steps: Stir the frozen berries straight into the cold yogurt — they firm it up as they thaw.
Mash a few against the side of the bowl to streak it pink, then stop stirring so it stays swirled.
Drizzle with honey and scatter granola over.

substitutions.use: a thick plant yogurt with maple syrup, for a vegan bowl

quickAlternatives.title: No-Bake Chocolate Oat Bites
quickAlternatives.description: Stirred together in one bowl, no oven, and they keep for a week.
steps: Stir everything together in a bowl until no dry oats remain. It should be stiff but hold together when squeezed.
If it crumbles, add honey a teaspoon at a time; if it is sticky, add more oats.
Roll into 12 balls and chill 20 minutes to firm up.

substitutions.use: any nut or seed butter
maple syrup makes these vegan

quickAlternatives.storage: Keeps a week in the fridge and freezes for 2 months.

quickAlternatives.title: Cheese, Crackers, and Fruit
quickAlternatives.description: A convenience-store shaped plate assembled at home in two minutes.
steps: Slice the cheese and fruit and arrange everything on one plate.
Eat with your hands. That is the whole recipe.

substitutions.use: hummus or a dairy-free cheese, for a vegan plate

quickAlternatives.title: Microwave Baked Potato
quickAlternatives.description: A whole hot meal from one potato and whatever is in the fridge, in about ten minutes.
steps: Prick the potato all over with a fork — at least eight times, or it can burst.
Microwave on full power for 5 minutes, turn it over, and microwave 3-5 minutes more.
It is done when a knife slides into the centre with no resistance. Give it 1-minute bursts if it is still firm.
Cut a cross in the top, squeeze the sides to open it, and add butter, salt, pepper, cheese, and beans.

substitutions.use: olive oil or a dairy-free spread; skip the cheese for a vegan potato
tinned tuna, leftover chilli, or nothing at all

quickAlternatives.title: Cottage Cheese Protein Bowl
quickAlternatives.description: High protein, no cooking, three minutes — savoury or sweet depending on what you add.

ingredients.item: fruit or diced tomato and cucumber

ingredients.note: oil for savoury, honey for sweet

steps: Spoon the cottage cheese into a bowl and flatten the top.
For savoury: add tomato and cucumber, olive oil, salt, and pepper. For sweet: add fruit and honey.
Scatter nuts or seeds over for texture.

substitutions.use: thick Greek yogurt, or a plant yogurt for a vegan bowl with maple syrup

quickAlternatives.storage: Eat straight away; keep cottage cheese refrigerated.

quickAlternatives.title: Frozen Wings in the Air Fryer
quickAlternatives.description: Straight from the freezer to crisp wings, with a sauce stirred together while they cook.
steps: Air fry the wings from frozen at 180 C / 350 F for 12 minutes to thaw them, shaking once.
Turn the heat to 200 C / 400 F and cook 10-12 minutes more, until the skin is deep golden and crisp and the thickest wing reads 74 C / 165 F.
Melt the butter with the hot sauce and honey, then toss the hot wings through it.

substitutions.use: oven at 220 C / 425 F on a wire rack for 40-45 minutes, turning twice
olive oil or a dairy-free spread

quickAlternatives.storage: Best fresh; re-crisp leftovers at 200 C / 400 F for 5 minutes.

quickAlternatives.title: Frozen Fries, Done Right
quickAlternatives.description: The bag you already have, cooked hot enough and spread thin enough to actually go crisp.
steps: Air fry at 200 C / 400 F for 14-16 minutes, or oven-bake at 220 C / 425 F for 20-22 minutes.
Spread them in one layer with gaps — a heaped basket steams instead of crisping — and shake once at the halfway point.
They are done when the outsides are deep golden and rigid rather than bendy.
Salt them the second they come out, while the surface is still hot enough for it to stick.

substitutions.use: frozen potato wedges or hash browns, adding 3-4 minutes
leave it out to keep this vegan

quickAlternatives.storage: Eat straight away; reheated fries never recover.

quickAlternatives.title: Coconut Curry Noodle Bowl
quickAlternatives.description: A simplified, Thai-inspired noodle broth from a tin of coconut milk and a spoon of curry paste.
steps: Fry the curry paste in a dry saucepan over medium heat for 60 seconds, until it darkens and smells fragrant.
Pour in the coconut milk and water, bring to a simmer, and add the frozen vegetables. Cook 5 minutes until they are tender and the broth is steaming hot.
Add the noodles and cook for the time on the packet, usually 3-4 minutes, until tender.
Take off the heat and stir in the lime juice and sugar.

substitutions.use: 1 tbsp curry powder with 1 tsp tomato paste; check the label, as many red and green pastes contain shrimp
any dried noodle, or leave them out and serve the broth over rice

quickAlternatives.storage: Keeps 2 days, though the noodles soften. Store the broth separately if you can.

quickAlternatives.title: Microwave Steamed Dumplings
quickAlternatives.description: Frozen dumplings with no pan and no stove — a bowl, a plate, and four minutes.
steps: Arrange the frozen dumplings in a single layer in a microwave-safe bowl and add the water.
Cover with a plate and microwave 3 minutes, then check one: it is ready when the wrapper is translucent and the filling is piping hot right through. Give it 30-second bursts if not.
Mix the soy sauce, vinegar, and chilli oil for dipping.

substitutions.use: vegetable dumplings, gyoza, or momos — check the packet if you need them vegetarian

quickAlternatives.title: Microwave Mug Pizza
quickAlternatives.description: A pizza-shaped answer for a kitchen with nothing but a microwave. Four minutes, one mug.
steps: Stir the flour, baking powder, milk, and oil together in a large microwave-safe mug until no dry flour is left in the corners.
Spoon the sauce over the top and scatter on the cheese — do not stir them in.
Microwave on full power for 80 seconds. It is done when the cheese has melted and the base has risen and looks set rather than wet.
Give it 10-second bursts if the middle is still batter, then sprinkle with oregano and let it stand 1 minute.

substitutions.use: any melting cheese or a dairy-free shred, which with plant milk makes it vegan
passata, or ketchup at a push

quickAlternatives.storage: Eat straight away; it goes tough as it cools.

quickAlternatives.title: Twelve-Minute Shoestring Fries
quickAlternatives.description: Thin-cut frozen fries crisp far faster than thick ones — the fastest honest chip there is.
steps: Spread the fries in a single loose layer in the air fryer basket. A heaped basket steams and will not crisp.
Air fry at 200 C / 400 F for 10-12 minutes, shaking hard twice.
They are done when they are deep golden and rigid rather than bendy — check one before you stop.
Salt them the moment they come out, while the surface is still hot enough for it to stick.

substitutions.use: thick-cut fries or wedges, adding 6-8 minutes
oven at 230 C / 450 F on a preheated tray for 16-18 minutes

quickAlternatives.storage: Eat straight away; reheated fries never recover.

quickAlternatives.title: No-Cook Bean Lettuce Tacos
quickAlternatives.description: Taco-shaped, crunchy, and nothing switched on at all. Six minutes.

ingredients.note: the cupped inner leaves hold best

steps: Mash about a third of the beans with the cumin and lime juice so the mixture holds together, then stir the rest through whole.
Spoon into the lettuce leaves and top with salsa and avocado.
Scatter the crushed chips over for crunch and eat with your hands.

substitutions.use: tortillas, or endive leaves; cabbage leaves work if you flatten the stem
any tinned bean, or tinned sweetcorn with the same seasoning

quickAlternatives.storage: The bean mix keeps 3 days; fill the leaves just before eating.

quickAlternatives.title: Cold Sesame Noodle Bowl
quickAlternatives.description: Built from noodles you already cooked. Nothing is heated, and it takes five minutes.
steps: Whisk the peanut butter, soy sauce, vinegar, and sesame oil in the bottom of a bowl. It will seize and look wrong.
Add the warm water a little at a time, whisking, until it loosens into a pourable sauce.
Add the cold noodles and toss until every strand is coated, then top with the shredded vegetables and chilli flakes.

substitutions.use: any leftover pasta, or rice noodles soaked in boiled water for 5 minutes
tahini or sunflower seed butter for a peanut-free bowl

quickAlternatives.storage: Keeps a day; the sauce thickens cold, so loosen with a splash of water.

quickAlternatives.title: Leftover Pasta Salad
quickAlternatives.description: Yesterday's pasta, turned into something you actually want, with no pan and no waiting.
steps: Whisk the oil, lemon juice, mustard, and salt in the bottom of a bowl until it thickens slightly.
Add the cold pasta and toss — cold pasta takes dressing far better than warm, which just absorbs it.
Fold through the vegetables, cheese, and olives, and let it sit 2 minutes before eating.

substitutions.use: a tin of drained chickpeas, which also makes it vegan
any leftover grain — rice, couscous, or bulgur

quickAlternatives.storage: Keeps 2 days in the fridge and travels well.

quickAlternatives.title: Miso Tofu Soup
quickAlternatives.description: A hot, savoury bowl from a kettle or a microwave in four minutes.
steps: Put the miso in a mug or bowl and add 3 tbsp of the hot water. Mash it with a spoon until completely smooth — miso will not dissolve once the bowl is full.
Add the rest of the water, the tofu, and the frozen vegetables.
Microwave 90 seconds, or leave it 2 minutes if the water came from a kettle. It is ready when it is steaming hot right through and the tofu has warmed.
Stir in the sesame oil if you have it, and scatter the spring onion over. Do not boil it — miso turns harsh and grainy above a simmer.

substitutions.use: a vegetable stock cube with 1 tsp soy sauce — different, but the same savoury bowl
a handful of frozen edamame, or leave it out and add noodles

quickAlternatives.title: Microwave Kimchi Rice Bowl
quickAlternatives.description: Sharp, spicy, and hot in five minutes with nothing but a microwave.

ingredients.note: roughly chopped, plus 2 tbsp of its juice

steps: Heat the rice pouch for the time on the packet, usually 2 minutes, until steaming hot.
Tip it into a bowl with the chopped kimchi and its juice and stir through.
Microwave 60 seconds more, until the kimchi has softened and the whole bowl is hot right through.
Stir in the sesame oil and soy sauce, then add the cheese and spring onion on top.

substitutions.use: sauerkraut with 1 tsp chilli flakes — different, but the same sharp-savoury effect
leave it out for a vegan bowl, and check your kimchi has no fish sauce

quickAlternatives.title: Chickpea Salad Sandwich
quickAlternatives.description: A plant substitute for a tuna sandwich — same texture, same mayonnaise, no fish.
steps: Mash the chickpeas with a fork until most are broken but some stay chunky — that texture is the whole point.
Stir in the mayonnaise, lemon juice, celery, and salt.
Pile onto the bread with the lettuce, close, and cut in half.

substitutions.use: ordinary mayonnaise, or mashed avocado with extra lemon
white beans, mashed the same way

quickAlternatives.storage: The filling keeps 3 days in the fridge.

quickAlternatives.title: Mango Lassi
quickAlternatives.description: Thick, cold, and sweet in three minutes — the drink to order alongside a curry, made at home.
steps: Put the milk in the blender first so the blades are not fighting frozen fruit from a standstill.
Add the yogurt, then the frozen mango on top, then the sweetener.
Blend 45-60 seconds until completely smooth and thick enough to hold the mark of a spoon.
Dust with cardamom and drink cold.

substitutions.use: a thick plant yogurt with sugar instead of honey, for a vegan lassi
tinned mango pulp with 4 ice cubes, or frozen peach

quickAlternatives.storage: Drink straight away; it separates as it warms.
